newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says air crash was due to engine failure.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says air crash was due to engine failure.

text.p: Cuban aviation authorities said on Wednesday engine failure was the most probable cause of last week's air crash in which a Cuban commercial plane plunged into the sea shortly after take-off, killing all 44 people on board.

A civil aviation institute statement said a state commission investigating the crash had determined the most likely scenario based on the technical history of the aircraft, the state of its crew, conditions at the time, experts' tests and witnesses' statements.

The Cubana de Aviacion plane, a Soviet-built twin-engined An-24, plunged into the sea minutes after take-off last Friday from the eastern city of Santiago de Cuba on a domestic flight to Havana. There were 39 passengers aboard, including six Spaniards and two Brazilians, and a crew of five.
Rescue workers have recovered 22 bodies from the sea, of which 21 have been identified.

The statement, published in the ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma, said a cockpit voice recorder from the plane had been recovered from the sea by rescue workers, but it had contributed nothing useful to the investigation.
The statement said the plane's flight recorder, which provides a record of technical data as the plane is flying, had not been found.
It said the investigation had ruled out weather conditions, air traffic control, land support services or the state of the airport at Santiago as possible causes of the crash.
"There is also no evidence that during the accident there were explosions or fire aboard the plane," the statement said.
It said the plane was in "correct technical order" and had the required maintenance history. The crew was both medically and technically fit to fly.
The investigation concluded the most likely cause of the crash was that the left engine of the plane failed during take-off, the statement said.

It said this difficulty could have been overcome, given the specifications of the plane and the experience of the crew. But the actions of the crew and the flight conditions meant it was impossible to prevent the crash, it said.

"The subsequent actions of the crew, in difficult conditions of low altitude, at low speed and flying at night, meant it was impossible to get out of the emergency and the plane fell into the sea," the statement said.
It gave no further details as to the cause of the accident.

The statement, which followed three brief communiques on the accident, was titled "final informative note." This meant Cuban authorities have now said as much as they are willing to say on the crash and are very unlikely to provide more details.
Cuba's worst airline disaster was in September 1989, when all 126 people aboard were killed when a Cubana plane crashed near Havana after taking off for Italy.
